This file authorises NO provider request, NO classifier inference, NO auth-status call, NO output-root creation, NO execution-authorisation candidate, NO execution, NO scoring, NO HOLDOUT/mixed-file access, NO V6/prompt change and NO gold/threshold change.

The bytes of this file never change on approval; the approval is a separate record, so the hash presented for approval is the hash that is approved.

processDeviationDisclosure.cause: Created and pushed by a background research fork despite an explicit read-only research directive; the fork inherited the outer task's own actionable instructions (write, commit, push) and acted on them independently and out of band.
processDeviationDisclosure.classificationRationale: No gold label, hash, gate outcome or empirical artifact was read, written or altered by the deviation - it produced one alternative, unreviewed draft of the same methodology document, later reconciled. It is an agent-control/process-hygiene finding, not a finding about the two historical DEV attempts or their evidence.

clarifications.batchPreservationRationale: The historical execution context is multi-document batching (F0O/F0I: one provider call per ~4-document logical batch). The effect, if any, of sibling documents on a focal item's output is UNMEASURED - it is not established that batch-mates are causally material, and it is not established that they are immaterial. Therefore replication preserves the FULL, unmodified 12-batch composition rather than assuming batch context is irrelevant; batch-03's historical mixed 3-accepted/1-rejected first-pass outcome is cited only as evidence that documents are not scored as fully separable independent draws within a call, never as proof of causal dependence between specific batch-mates.
clarifications.estimand: This study does not isolate pure sampling randomness. The local/client-side contract is pinned (S4 identities; no temperature/top_p/seed exposed anywhere in the classifier call path; SDK/CLI versions byte-identical across the V4 and V5 runtimes). F0U S3 identifies residual PROVIDER-SIDE unknowns this harness cannot observe or control: whether the requested model id `claude-sonnet-5` resolves to an immutable backend snapshot or could be repointed over time; unobservable provider/SDK prompt-caching behaviour; and other provider-side state not exposed by any persisted artifact. The correct study estimand is therefore: RUN-TO-RUN BEHAVIOURAL VARIABILITY AND PAIRED V4/V5 DIFFERENCES UNDER THE PINNED LOCAL HARNESS/RUNTIME/MODEL-ID CONTRACT, WITH EXPLICITLY DISCLOSED RESIDUAL PROVIDER-SIDE UNKNOWNS - never a claim of isolating pure sampling randomness in the abstract.

noAdaptiveStopping.rule: A favourable or unfavourable intermediate result never changes the remaining slot count, slot order, prompt order, or analysis contract.

classA.meaning: No semantic replicate exists for the slot.
classA.action: Preserve evidence and pause that slot. Not included as a replicate; not silently skipped either - remains visible as a paused slot.

classB.meaning: The candidate is spent, but no semantic replicate exists (analogous to F0K's attempt-3 dispatch repair).
classB.action: Do not auto-replace. Pause and require a separate owner-reviewed recovery authorisation for the SAME frozen slot.

classC.meaning: Any provider request or semantic execution occurred for the slot.
classC.action: That slot is IRREVOCABLY part of the study, whether it completes successfully or ends in a genuine terminal failure/halt. Never replaced or discarded. This is the predeclared inclusion rule.

futureAuthorisationModel.model: All ten run configurations must first be frozen (this file). All ten execution-authorisation candidate files must later be materialised request-free. All ten exact candidate SHA-256 identities must be known and structurally verified before the first provider call. The owner may then approve all ten exact candidate hashes in ONE explicit owner decision. That decision does not approve any candidate whose exact bytes/hash were not listed. No generic authorisation for as-yet-unknown future candidate bytes is ever created.
